deed: גולדה מאיר מקימה את מש״ב, סוכנות ישראלית שמכשירה מדינות מתפתחות
title: Golda Meir returned from Africa and founded MASHAV, which has trained hundreds of thousands of people in developing countries

trailer.text: Golda Meir, Israel's foreign minister, returned in 1958 from a tour of Africa and spoke of Israel's determination to assist the new African states in their economic development.
According to Gil Haskel, head of MASHAV, Meir went into the communities herself during the trip, and came back with a deep conviction of the need to establish an international development agency.
In 1958 she established a section for technical cooperation in her ministry, which became MASHAV, Israel's national aid agency.
MASHAV provides training and consulting to developing countries in agriculture, health, education and women's empowerment.
According to the MASHAV website, it has since trained about 300,000 men and women from across the developing world.

glance.label: Where
glance.value: A division of Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: About 300,000 graduates, according to the MASHAV website

paragraphs.text: According to the Forward, in 1958 Israel was a young state struggling to absorb refugees.
According to Wikipedia, Israel was not invited to the Bandung Conference in 1955 at the demand of Arab countries, which threatened to boycott the conference if Israel was invited.

Following the decision not to invite Israel to the Bandung Conference, policy makers realized that they must pay more attention to third world countries and develop ties with the emerging African countries.
Even earlier, in 1953, David Hacohen was sent to Burma as Israel's first envoy.
He was one of the fathers of the technical cooperation programs.
According to the JCPA article, the Jewish people, who had suffered discrimination and persecution, felt a closeness to the peoples of Africa, who had suffered discrimination and the slave trade.
According to the JCPA article, early in 1958 Meir visited Africa for the first time: Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Ghana and the Ivory Coast.
According to Haskel, she went into the communities herself to see what the challenges were.
Haskel told the Jerusalem Post that Meir returned horrified at the poverty and at the way women were treated.
Already then she spoke of Israel's determination to assist the new African states.
Ambassador Yaakov Tsur, who accompanied her on the tour, told newsmen that a number of African ministers in the French territories had been invited to visit Israel.
According to the Times of Israel, Meir persuaded Ben-Gurion that Israel had a moral and political obligation to share knowledge with young nations.
In 1958 Meir established a section for technical cooperation in her ministry, headed by Hanan Aynor.
According to the MASHAV website, this happened ten years after the Declaration of Independence, according to Ben-Gurion's vision and at Meir's initiative.
In 1960 the section became an independent department, whose name was later changed to the Center for International Cooperation, MASHAV.
MASHAV was established before USAID and before the United Nations Development Programme.
According to Peter Pham, it was founded more than five years before USAID began operating.
In the first year, 1958-9, 137 course participants came to Israel, and eighty Israeli experts were sent abroad.

stations.title: To teach, not to give money

paragraphs.text: Israel was one of the first countries to aid the African states immediately after their independence.
This aid was not necessarily given in the form of cash grants, and often consisted mainly of manpower training.
Haskel explained that Israel had no natural resources and faced many security challenges, and therefore has unique experience to give.
MASHAV had clear principles.
To start with small and medium-sized projects rather than showcase projects.
The Israeli experts leave when the locals can continue on their own.
And aid is not conditioned on political considerations.
Between 1958 and 1971, 4,341 experts served MASHAV, and 2,763 of them were sent to Africa.
Until 1973, 34 ophthalmologists were sent to Africa, in a project of Prof. Michaelson.
In the 1960s MASHAV helped build hospitals, airports, universities and roads in almost every country in Africa.
There were so many Israeli experts there that two schools were set up for their children, in East Africa and in West Africa.

stations.title: A center for women on Mount Carmel

paragraphs.text: In 1961 MASHAV's first training center opened, on Mount Carmel.
This is the Golda Meir Mount Carmel International Training Center, which was intended to train women from developing countries.
According to the Jerusalem Post, it was the first institution in the world to deal with the empowerment of women.
According to Haskel, that same year Meir organized an international conference for women, and invited 66 women from all over the world.
According to the MASHAV website, since its founding it has trained about 300,000 men and women.
According to an article in The Jerusalem Post, at the time of its writing each course lasted about three to four weeks, and participants came from 140 countries.
According to Haskel, the graduates include ministers, foreign ministers, members of parliament, judges and police officers in large numbers.
About half of the work is carried out in the poverty-stricken areas of Africa, and it has also expanded to Latin America, Nepal, Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos.
In countries that were part of the Soviet Union, Israeli experts trained the residents in emergency preparedness and post-trauma treatment.
According to Pham, in the 1950s and 1960s Israel was one of the most active countries in Africa, with ambassadors in 33 countries.
In 2009 Israel had diplomatic relations with 40 countries in Africa.
In December 2017 MASHAV signed a memorandum of understanding with USAID to join the Power Africa program.
Meir wrote in her autobiography that she was more proud of the international cooperation program and the assistance to Africa than of any other project.
Abba Eban said that MASHAV's aid should be seen in its human context, and not as a political tool.
According to the Atlantic Council article, MASHAV has helped nations in need for six decades.
A book marking 60 years of MASHAV describes how tiny Israel has put the Jewish principle of Tikkun Olam into practice.
African countries began severing relations with Israel in the 1970s, and the process peaked in 1973.
When Zambia severed relations, Israel brought home the eight experts who were running an agricultural project there.
Israel sharply cut its aid budget in 1973.
After the severing of ties it was claimed that MASHAV had failed and had not prevented Israel from being thrown out of most of the African countries.
Hanan Aynor admitted in a lecture that MASHAV was not completely altruistic, and that Israel was isolated and needed friends.
The Forward also wrote that Israel hoped to win international support and to lessen its isolation.
Among Israelis there was a demand to condition aid on a position sympathetic toward Israel, and the policy makers rejected it.
Haskel said that Israel does not condition its aid, but does expect friendship.

Israel's ambassador to Guatemala, Matti Cohen, said that he had no doubt that Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernandez's decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital was influenced by his visit to Israel as a young man to take part in a MASHAV course on leadership.
Cohen said that MASHAV graduates in El Salvador supported Israel during Operation Cast Lead.
But according to a newspaper, a link between a MASHAV course and a favorable attitude toward Jerusalem cannot be proven.

Fatou Bensouda, the Chief Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, took part in a MASHAV conference, and in December she announced that there was a “reasonable basis” to open a war crimes investigation concerning Israeli military actions in the Gaza Strip and Hamas, as well as Israeli construction in the settlements in the West Bank.
According to the Jerusalem Post, MASHAV is totally dependent on the state budget.
In 2007 only four Israelis were working in three African countries on long-term missions.

According to an article in The Times of Israel, in the year before its publication MASHAV went through its biggest financial crisis up to that time, which forced it to cut back its overseas activities almost to zero, although most of the courses in Israel continued.
Israel is low on the list of OECD countries in the scale of its aid.

According to a joint study by Tel Aviv University and the Pears Foundation, cited in an article from the period when Israel still hoped to join the OECD, Israel then spent only 0.048% of its gross national income on development assistance.
Since joining the OECD in 2010 it must dedicate part of its budget to aid, and it still does not meet the target.
According to the Jerusalem Post article, the director of the Carmel Center visited Africa ten years after its founding, and saw that nothing had changed.

claims.text: כשזמביה ניתקה יחסים ב-1973, ישראל החזירה הביתה את צוות שמונת המומחים שניהל את הפרויקט החקלאי.
claims.quote: When Zambia cut off diplomatic relations with Israel in 1973, Israel brought home the eight-man team of experts running the project.

claims.text: ישראל קיצצה בחדות בתקציב הסיוע ב-1973, כשרבים מהנהנים ניתקו יחסים בעקבות מלחמת יום הכיפורים.
claims.quote: Israel slashed its foreign aid budget drastically in 1973, when many of the beneficiaries of its assistance sided with the Arabs and severed ties with Jerusalem

claims.text: לאחר הניתוק נטען שמש״ב נכשלה ולא מנעה את גירוש ישראל ממרבית מדינות אפריקה.
claims.quote: It was claimed that MASHAV had failed to achieve its goals and had not prevented Israel from being thrown out of most of the African countries.

claims.text: חנן אינור הודה בהרצאה שמש״ב לא הייתה אלטרואיסטית לחלוטין, ושישראל הייתה מבודדת פוליטית וזקוקה לחברים.
claims.quote: MASHAV was not completely altruistic. Countries and the relations between them are never altruistic. As a country we were politically isolated and we needed friends.

claims.text: המאמר מציין שיוזמת ישראל לא הייתה אלטרואיסטית לגמרי: ישראל קיוותה שהיא תזכה לתמיכה בינלאומית ותפחית את בידודה הפוליטי.
claims.quote: Of course, Israel’s initiative wasn’t completely selfless. It hoped that its outreach program would garner international support and help lessen its political isolation.

claims.text: בקרב ישראלים נשמעה הדרישה להתנות סיוע בעמדה אוהדת לישראל, והדבר נדחה על ידי קובעי המדיניות.
claims.quote: Several Israeli ambassadors to Africa, members of the Knesset, and the Israeli media demanded that aid be conditioned on a position sympathetic toward Israel.

claims.text: חסקל אמר שישראל אינה מתנה את הסיוע, אך רואה בו עדות לידידות וגם מצפה לידידות ולמערכת יחסים טובה.
claims.quote: But without conditioning it, we do see the whole process of development cooperation as a testimony of friendship and good relations

claims.text: שגריר ישראל בגואטמלה מתי כהן הניח שהחלטת נשיא הונדורס להכיר בירושלים הושפעה מקורס מש״ב שלקח בו חלק.
claims.quote: has no doubt that Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernandez’s decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel’s capital was influenced by his visit to Israel as a young man to take part in a MASHAV course on leadership.

claims.text: בוגרים לשעבר של מש״ב באל סלבדור כתבו מאמרים והפגינו תמיכה בישראל במהלך מבצע עופרת יצוקה, כך סיפר כהן.
claims.quote: but former MASHAV graduates in the country stepped up to write newspaper articles and to demonstrate in support of the Jewish state.

claims.text: לפי עיתון, אי אפשר להוכיח קשר סיבתי בין חוויית מש״ב של בכירים ליחס אוהד לירושלים.
claims.quote: Causal links cannot, of course, be proven between the MASHAV experiences of people who have gone onto senior positions in their countries and favorable attitudes to Jerusalem

claims.text: פאטו בנסודה, תובעת בית הדין הפלילי הבינלאומי, השתתפה בכנס של מש״ב ובדצמבר הודיעה על בסיס סביר לפתוח בחקירה על פשעי מלחמה ישראליים.
claims.quote: she announced that there was a “reasonable basis” to open a war crimes probe into Israeli military actions in the Gaza Strip and Hamas

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, מש״ב תלויה כליל בתקציב המדינה.
claims.quote: but the organization is totally dependent on the state budget's allotting them enough money.

claims.text: ב-2007 עבדו רק ארבעה ישראלים בשלוש מדינות באפריקה במשימות ארוכות טווח.
claims.quote: in 2007 only 4 Israelis were working in three African countries in such frameworks.

claims.text: השנה שעברה סבלה מש״ב ממשבר הכספי הגדול ביותר שלה, שאילץ אותה לצמצם את פעילותה בחו״ל כמעט לאפס.
claims.quote: Last year, the organization suffered its biggest financial crisis to date which forced it to cut back its overseas activities almost to zero.

claims.text: ישראל נמצאת נמוך ברשימת מדינות ה-OECD בהיקף הסיוע לעולם המתפתח.
claims.quote: These days, Israel comes low on the list of OECD nations in the aid it provides to developing countries.

claims.text: בהיקף שנתי, ישראל מוציאה רק 0.048% מההכנסה הלאומית הגולמית על סיוע פיתוח, לפי מחקר של אוניברסיטת תל אביב וקרן פירס.
claims.quote: Israel currently spends only 0.048% of its gross national income on overseas development assistance.

claims.text: בעקבות הצטרפותה של ישראל ל-OECD ב-2010 עליה להקדיש חלק מתקציבה לסיוע חוץ, אך היא עדיין אינה עומדת ביעד שנקבע.
claims.quote: בשל הצטרפותה של ישראל ב-2010 לארגון ה-OECD עליה להקדיש חלק מתקציבה לסיוע חוץ , אך עדיין אינה עומדת ביעד שנקבע.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, מנהלת המרכז ביקרה באפריקה עשר שנים לאחר הקמתו, ונוכחה שדבר לא השתנה.
claims.quote: She was discouraged and frustrated to see that absolutely nothing had changed.

claims.text: לפי טיימס אוף ישראל, מש״ב הכשירה עד היום יותר מ-300,000 איש מ-140 מדינות מתפתחות.
claims.quote: MASHAV has to date trained more than 300,000 people from 140 nations in the developing world.

claims.text: לפי מאמר JCPA, מאז הקמתה ב-1958 העניקה מש״ב הדרכה מקצועית ל-230,000 משתתפי קורסים מ-140 מדינות מתפתחות.
claims.quote: Since its establishment in 1958 it has provided professional guidance for 230,000 course participants from 140 developing countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, מאז הקמתה השתתפו בהכשרות מש״ב מעל 270,000 אנשי מקצוע מיותר מ-132 מדינות.
claims.quote: Since its establishment, over 270,000 professionals from more than 132 countries have participated in Mashav's training programs.

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, עד 2010 הכשירה מש״ב רבע מיליון תלמידים, ברובם אפריקאים.
claims.quote: By 2010, Mashav had trained a quarter of a million students, predominantly African

claims.text: לפי גיל חסקל, ראש מש״ב, הסוכנות נולדה מנסיעתה של שרת החוץ הישראלית גולדה מאיר לאפריקה ב-1957.
claims.quote: the agency was born out of a trip by then-Israeli foreign minister Golda Meir to Africa in 1957

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, מש״ב החלה בסוף 1957 לשתף ידע וטכנולוגיות שעמדו בבסיס ההתפתחות המהירה של ישראל.
claims.quote: Since its inception in late 1957, Mashav has striven to share with the rest of the developing world the know-how and technologies

claims.text: לפי טיימס אוף ישראל, לאחר מלחמת יום הכיפורים 1973 כל מדינות אפריקה פרט לארבע ניתקו יחסים עם ישראל.
claims.quote: Thus, all but four African countries cut off relations with Israel after the 1973 Yom Kippur

quote_translations.c1: is a division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and serves as Israel's national aid agency, responsible for formulating, leading and implementing the policy of foreign aid to developing countries
quote_translations.c3: MASHAV conducts trainings and consulting for developing countries on various subjects in which Israel has a relative advantage: agriculture in all its components, health, education, women's empowerment
quote_translations.c4: Since its founding MASHAV has trained about 300,000 thousand men and women from across the developing world
quote_translations.c2: It was founded in 1958, only ten years after Israel's declaration of independence, according to the vision of the first prime minister, Ben-Gurion, and at the initiative of the then foreign minister, Golda Meir.
quote_translations.c5: Because of Israel's joining the OECD in 2010, it must dedicate part of its budget to foreign aid, but it still does not meet the target that was set.
